Review Title: Very disappointed with Booking.com’s…
Review Text: Very disappointed with Booking.com’s Price Match Guarantee. I found the exact same holiday home, for the exact same dates, on the property management agency’s website for approximately €550 less. I still chose to book through Booking.com because I have used the platform for years and trusted their advertised Price Match Guarantee. I submitted a price match claim, but Booking.com is now refusing it because they say the property is “no longer available” on the other website. But this is ONE holiday home — not a hotel with multiple identical rooms. Of course it is no longer available for the same dates once it has been booked! This makes absolutely no sense. If Booking.com requires a unique property to remain available after it has been reserved in order to honour a Price Match claim, then how is the Price Match Guarantee supposed to work for holiday homes with only one unit? The price difference was around €550. Had I known Booking.com would handle the claim this way, I would simply have booked directly with the property management agency and saved €550. I chose Booking.com specifically because I trusted the platform and its Price Match promise. Unfortunately, this experience has seriously damaged that trust. I would like Booking.com to properly review the evidence and honour the Price Match Guarantee they advertise.

Review Title: I would avoid this company at all…
Review Text: I would avoid this company at all costs. A phishing link was sent to me through Booking.com's own messaging system, and it took me finding the evidence myself to get anyone to act I booked a London apartment through Booking.com for August. After I confirmed the reservation, a message came through Booking.com's own platform directing me to an external website to enter my card details. Booking.com's published guidance is that they never ask guests to do this. What I then found, entirely on my own: 1. The contact number given for a London property was a US number. 2. The host did not respond for four days, not to my messages, not to Booking.com's messages, and not to a phone call Booking.com made to them. 3. The address given for the apartment is a pub. There is no apartment there. 4. The Booking.com listing page for the property is titled as a holiday cottage in Somerset, not the London apartment I had booked. None of this was flagged by Booking.com. I found all of it. One agent even told me the property was legitimate with strong reviews, apparently reading review history that had nothing to do with what I had booked. The support experience was worse than the fraud: 1. I was given three different timeframes in a single day. First 48 hours, then three hours, then no timeframe at all. 2. A live chat was closed on me while I still had unanswered questions. 3. One agent confirmed in writing that relocation would be arranged free of charge. A second agent confirmed relocation was guaranteed. A third then told me the approved support was €25. 4. I was told Booking.com would not book replacement accommodation directly, and that I should fund a replacement myself and claim back afterwards. 5. The alternative eventually offered was student accommodation in zone 4, priced below my original booking so that Booking.com contributed nothing at all. 6. Any shortfall would be paid as Travel Credits to spend with Booking.com, not as money. Fraudulent listings appear on every large platform. That is not the problem. The problem is that a phishing attempt was delivered through Booking.com's own systems, that the listing did not match its own page, that none of it was detected until a customer did the work, and that the response was to offer €25 and a suggestion I pay for it myself.

Review Title: Fraudulent Advertising & selling of Car Sizes - Booking.com confirmed a 7-seater, then left my family without suitable transport days before travel
Review Text: In February 2026 I booked and paid for a car through Booking.com specifically because the car advertised and sold clearly stated “Volvo XC90 or similar – 7 seats.” We are travelling as three adults and three young children, so seven seats were an essential requirement of the booking. Less than one week before our holiday, I downloaded the rental voucher and discovered that Booking.com had changed the reservation to a BMW X5 showing only 5 seats. I immediately contacted Booking.com. Since then, multiple members of their own team have acknowledged in writing that: • My original Booking.com confirmation shows 7 seats. • The vehicle currently associated with my booking is a 5-seater. • They cannot confirm that Hertz will provide a 7-seat vehicle. Despite acknowledging the discrepancy, Booking.com has repeatedly suggested that I: * cancel my booking and rebook at today’s peak-season prices; * contact their supplier in France myself; * or arrive at Marseille Airport with three young children and simply refuse the vehicle if it is unsuitable. None of these is a reasonable solution. I booked six months in advance to avoid exactly this situation. I have now spent many hours speaking to multiple agents, sending evidence repeatedly and explaining the same issue over and over again. Every representative apologises. Every representative agrees there is a problem. Yet nobody has taken ownership or provided a solution. Five days before travel I still have no confirmation that my family will actually have transport capable of carrying all six of us. I have retained the complete documentary evidence, including: • the original 7-seat confirmation; • the later 5-seat voucher; • the full live chat transcript; • and Booking.com’s written acknowledgements that the booking no longer matches the original confirmation. I sincerely hope Booking.com resolves this before we travel. If they do, I will happily update this review. At present, however, I cannot recommend using Booking.com for car hire where vehicle specifications are critical.

Review Title: Avoid Gotogate by Booking.com at All Costs
Review Text: My experience with Gotogate by Booking.com has been one of the most frustrating and stressful travel experiences I've ever had. I strongly advise anyone considering booking through them to think twice. Our Thai Lion Air flight was cancelled by the airline on 3 June, well in advance of our scheduled travel on 2 July. However, we were never informed by Gotogate or Booking.com that our flight had been cancelled. There was no email, no SMS, no phone call, and no attempt to offer an alternative flight or assist us in any way. The only reason we discovered the cancellation was when we tried to complete web check-in before our trip. Imagine the shock and panic of finding out that your flight doesn't even exist just days before your vacation. Because of this complete failure in communication, we were forced to book expensive last-minute replacement tickets, costing us significantly more than what we had originally paid. The worst part began after that. It has now been over two months, and despite countless follow-ups, we have still not received our refund. Every single time we contact Gotogate, we are given the same scripted response: "We are waiting for the airline to refund us." They refuse to take any ownership of the issue or provide any meaningful update. To make matters worse, they repeatedly provide incorrect information, claiming that the flight was cancelled on 3 July, when in reality it was cancelled on 3 June. Even after correcting them multiple times, they continue to rely on inaccurate records instead of investigating the matter properly. As the company that accepted my payment and issued my booking, Gotogate/Booking.com should be accountable to their customers. Passing all responsibility to the airline while leaving customers without information, assistance, or refunds is simply unacceptable. Customers should not be expected to bear the financial burden and uncertainty because an intermediary fails to do its job. The entire experience has caused unnecessary financial loss, countless hours spent chasing customer support, and tremendous mental stress. Every interaction has felt like talking to a wall, with no accountability, no empathy, and no resolution. I have completely lost trust in Gotogate and Booking.com for flight bookings. Saving a small amount on a ticket is not worth the risk of being abandoned when something goes wrong. My advice to anyone considering booking flights through Gotogate or Booking.com: Don't. Book directly with the airline or use a travel agency that actually supports its customers. If your flight gets cancelled, be prepared for poor communication, endless excuses, delayed refunds, and zero accountability. This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had, and I will never use Gotogate or Booking.com for flight bookings again. I will also actively recommend that my friends, family, and colleagues avoid them if they value their money, time, and peace of mind.

Review Title: Booking.com abandoned its customers…
Review Text: Booking.com abandoned its customers during an extreme emergency I had used Booking.com for many years and made numerous reservations through the platform. However, its conduct during the catastrophic wildfires around Arcachon has completely destroyed my confidence in the company. Our family had booked two rooms near Arcachon Bay. At that time, the area was being affected by some of the largest wildfires in modern French history. Major access roads were closed, mass evacuations were taking place, and the Gironde authorities were asking tourists not to travel to the affected region. Arcachon Bay was effectively situated between two major fire zones. Despite the extraordinary scale of the emergency, Booking.com apparently did not classify the area as being affected by an extreme or emergency situation. It did not issue us any meaningful warning and, when we asked for assistance, simply distanced itself from the problem. The hotel’s position was predictable: it wanted to keep the money, even though no accommodation service was provided. But Booking.com’s attitude towards its customers was truly shocking. Its customer service merely told us that nothing could be done because the hotel refused to authorise a refund. I am certain that our family was not the only one planning a holiday around Arcachon Bay at that time. Booking.com’s failure to recognise the seriousness of the situation and its refusal to provide any meaningful assistance are therefore extremely difficult to understand. Booking.com was perfectly willing to act as an intermediary when accepting the reservation and benefiting commercially from it. However, when a genuine emergency occurred and its customers needed protection, the company simply stepped aside and accepted no responsibility. After many years as a loyal customer, I can only say that Booking.com disgraced itself in this situation. Before making my next hotel reservation, I will think very carefully about whether to use Booking.com again. At the very least, travellers should not expect any real assistance from the platform when something serious goes wrong.

Review Title: Avoid and find an alternative
Review Text: I have had an absolutely awful experience with Booking.com and I am still trying to get my money back. I booked a property through Booking.com, but before my stay the property owners began demanding an additional €150 payment and told me I would not be allowed into the building unless I paid it. This was extremely concerning, particularly after I checked the property’s reviews and found multiple guests reporting problems getting their €150 “deposit” returned. The property had also received a significant number of very negative reviews. Because of this, I contacted Booking.com at around midday on 31 July, BEFORE booking alternative accommodation. I asked them for help and reassurance about the situation. I received no resolution or meaningful assistance. As I could not risk arriving with nowhere safe to stay, I eventually booked another hotel. On the day of my original booking, the property refused to let me enter because I would not pay the additional €150. They also refused to cancel my booking. I contacted Booking.com again, extremely upset, and explained what had happened. I was told that I would receive approximately a quarter of my money back once the booking period had ended. Even this seemed completely inadequate considering I had paid for accommodation that I was not permitted to access. I have now contacted Booking.com to claim the refund I was promised, only to be told that I am not entitled to it because I supposedly booked my replacement hotel BEFORE reporting the problem. This is simply not true. I have evidence showing that I contacted Booking.com on 31 July before booking the alternative accommodation. Booking.com therefore had the opportunity to assist me before I was forced to make alternative arrangements, but failed to do so. I had previously had good experiences booking hotels through Booking.com, but this was the first time I actually needed their customer service to resolve a serious problem. The experience has completely changed my opinion of the company. When something went wrong, I received virtually no meaningful support, was left to find alternative accommodation myself, and am now being refused even the partial refund I was previously told I would receive. I would strongly recommend booking directly with hotels or using another provider. My experience has shown me that when a serious problem occurs with a property, you cannot necessarily rely on Booking.com to protect you or help you recover your money. I am still requesting that Booking.com review the evidence, honour the refund I was promised and resolve this properly.

Review Title: Booking.com is a terrible platform
Review Text: Booking.com is a terrible platform that had repeatedly failed me when I needed customer service I have used Booking.com extensively, but my experience following a serious incident at a property has completely changed my view of the company. I booked four nights at Westbury House in Windermere through Booking.com. I physically attended the property within the stated check-in period, with my luggage, and attempted to check in. Following an extraordinary confrontation with the owners, the door was closed on me while I was still standing at the threshold. I was not admitted and received none of the four nights I had paid for. What happened afterwards with Booking.com was almost as appalling. I spent approximately two hours making around 16 calls to Booking.com numbers in Australia, the UK and the Netherlands trying to report what had happened. Calls repeatedly disconnected, including after I had been placed on hold, meaning I had to call back, identify myself and start explaining everything again. One agent, Mohammed, became embroiled in a pointless argument about my reservation number, despite ultimately acknowledging that he could already identify the booking. When I asked for a supervisor, he refused to escalate the call. I called again and spoke with Christine. After I criticised the lack of empathy and customer service I was receiving, she actually told me: “I’m hanging up on you. You have to call back. I don’t like the way you’re speaking to me.” And she did. Meanwhile, Booking.com was emailing me saying it had contacted the property about my complaint even though nobody had successfully taken my complete account of what had happened. I replied asking, “How can you have advised them when I have not told you a thing?” and repeatedly asked for someone to call me. I then pursued Booking.com through email and X/Twitter, including providing a detailed written account. I was repeatedly redirected back towards the same telephone customer-service system that had already failed me. Now comes perhaps the most disturbing part: despite my repeatedly telling Booking.com that I physically attended Westbury House and had the door closed on me at the threshold, I have apparently been recorded as a NO-SHOW. That is simply false. And conveniently, being classified as a no-show means I am now unable to leave a Booking.com review of the property and what happened to me there. So I attended the property, was refused the accommodation, spent hours trying to report what happened, experienced repeated disconnections and failed escalation, sent written complaints explaining that I had attended — and I am now prevented from reviewing the property because the booking records incorrectly say I never showed up. Whether Booking.com or the property disputes my entitlement to a refund is one issue. Whether I attended the property is another. I did attend. I was not a no-show. A booking platform proves its value when something goes wrong. Taking a reservation and processing payment is easy. Providing meaningful assistance when a customer is standing outside accommodation they have paid for is where customer service actually matters. In my experience, Booking.com failed spectacularly at precisely that point.

Review Title: Booking.com allowed a completely fake listing onto its site and it has cost me dearly.
Review Text: Do not trust this platform with your family holidays or your personal data. I booked an apartment in Paris (Le Grand Paris Apartments, Reservation 6142145566) for a family holiday. Shortly after, the scammers contacted me directly inside Booking.com’s own platform messaging system and via official-looking emails demanding payment and identity verification. Because the request came through Booking.com’s trusted channels, I uploaded a scan of my driver's license. The scammers then immediately sent demands for external payments via third-party links. When I investigated further, past guest reviews exposed the horrific truth: previous guests turned up to find they had no booking, and reviews showed a horse-drawn ive in waggon in an empty field instead of a luxury Paris apartment, leaving families stranded. Booking.com openly allowed a completely fraudulent vendor onto their platform and enabled them to use internal messaging tools to trap customers. Because of Booking.com’s utter failure to secure their platform our family holiday is in ruins, and we are left stranded with no accommodation in Paris. Scammers now possess my full name, home address, date of birth, email address, age and a scan of my driver's license. I had to pay £30 for CIFAS Protective Registration to prevent fraudulent bank accounts from being opened in my name, over £20 for a replacement driver's license, and cancel my credit card. Hours of Administrative Stress and I have had to spend hours filing criminal police reports with Action Fraud and setting up fraud monitoring. When I confronted customer support about this nightmare, the agent offered zero accountability, gave copy-paste advice on running antivirus scans, and abruptly ended the chat while I was still speaking. Booking.com allowed criminals to exploit their internal system, handed over my personal data to fraudsters, destroyed our family holiday, and dumped 100% of the cost and stress onto me. Use this site at your own extreme risk. Hours after I made a complaint and was told they were investigating the listing, I went on to Booking.com becasue I was curious. Le Grand Paris Apartments, with its fake photos and fake reviews, is back online and fully capable of taking bookings. After everything I went through, I find that unbelievable and unacceptable.

Review Title: Promised a refund, now being offered Travel Credit
Review Text: Extremely disappointing experience with Booking.com. We booked an apartment in Nice but were informed there was a leak and were offered an alternative apartment further away from the city centre. We said we wanted to keep that option open while seeing whether something closer was available. Instead, our booking was cancelled, leaving us without accommodation and having to spend a considerable amount of time contacting Booking.com. When we eventually spoke to a representative, we were told we could choose alternative accommodation and that Booking.com would refund the difference in price. We selected more expensive accommodation in the centre and then received written confirmation from Booking.com stating: “We will cover up the price difference up to the amount EUR 336.39.” Based on both the telephone conversation and this written confirmation, we booked the more expensive accommodation, which cost €882.96. We would not have chosen accommodation at this price had we not been assured that Booking.com would cover the difference. After our stay, Booking.com asked us to provide an invoice in order to process the reimbursement. Their subsequent email repeatedly referred to this as a refund, including: “To proceed with your refund request…” “We’ll be happy to move forward with your refund.” And most clearly: “Once we receive this, we will promptly process the refund for you.” Despite all of this, we are now being told that the price difference will NOT be refunded and can only be provided as Booking.com Travel Credit towards a future booking. What makes this even more frustrating is that Booking.com clearly knows the distinction between a refund and Travel Credit. In the original email, they separately stated that if we incurred “additional charges at the new place”, they could “look into adding Travel Credits to your Wallet.” Travel Credits were therefore specifically mentioned in relation to additional charges, but NOT when Booking.com told us they would “cover” the price difference. We were also verbally told it would be a refund and subsequently received an email referring to the payment as a “refund” multiple times. Had we been told from the outset that we would have to pay the additional cost ourselves and receive credit towards a future Booking.com reservation instead, we would NEVER have chosen the more expensive accommodation. Customer service throughout this process has also been incredibly frustrating. Telephone waiting times are very long, getting through to someone who can actually help is extremely difficult, and we have even had calls cut off after waiting, forcing us to start the process again. We aren't asking for anything extra. We simply want Booking.com to honour what we were repeatedly told, both verbally and in writing, and reimburse the agreed price difference, up to the €336.39 maximum confirmed in their email. Travel Credit requiring us to book with Booking.com again is not the same as the refund we were repeatedly told we would receive. I will happily update this review if Booking.com honours the reimbursement we were promised and resolves the matter.

Review Title: Extremely disappointing experience1 STAR — BOOKING.COM LEFT ME £5,000+ OUT OF POCKET AFTER GUEST DAMAGE with…
Review Text: Extremely disappointing experience with Booking.com and their handling of serious property damage. I had guests stay at my property, Monkleigh House, who caused significant damage during their stay, including serious flooding. The total damage was in excess of £5,000. There were also issues with the number of guests. The guests arrived with more people than were included in the original reservation. Rather than cancelling their booking and ruining their stay, we tried to resolve the situation reasonably and allowed the booking to continue after agreeing that the additional guests would be paid for. After they checked out, we discovered extensive damage to the property. We provided Booking.com with photographs, evidence and contractor information demonstrating the extent of the damage. And what did Booking.com do? They simply sent a payment request to the guest. The guest said they didn't agree to pay it. And that was effectively the end of the process. Despite the damage being supported by evidence and the costs being thousands of pounds, Booking.com offered no meaningful solution and no effective mechanism for recovering the money. What makes this even more frustrating is that Booking.com controls the booking process and charges commission on every reservation, yet when a guest causes thousands of pounds worth of damage, the responsibility appears to be pushed entirely back onto the property owner. Their damage deposit system is also completely inadequate. The maximum deposit they allow for the property is nowhere near sufficient to cover serious damage. In my case, the actual loss was over £5,000. What is the point of having a damage claim process if a guest can simply say "I don't agree" and the platform effectively washes its hands of the matter? As a property owner, I accepted the booking through Booking.com in good faith and relied on their platform to provide a reasonable level of protection when something goes seriously wrong. Instead, I have been left with a substantial financial loss and a damaged property. This isn't about trying to avoid paying for legitimate damage or making an unreasonable claim. The damage was real, substantial and documented. The problem is that Booking.com's system appears to be designed to make it easy to book a property, while leaving the property owner carrying the financial risk when a guest causes serious damage. Very disappointing treatment of property owners. If you operate a property through Booking.com, I would strongly recommend understanding exactly how little protection you may actually have when a guest causes significant damage. For me, this experience has seriously damaged my confidence in Booking.com as a platform for property owners.

Review Title: Very disappointing and misleading…
Review Text: Very disappointing and misleading experience with Booking.com. That is not what I expected when making a reservation so far in advance. The entire process felt deceptive: take the card information to secure the reservation, immediately charge the full amount, and then inform the customer that the booking is essentially locked. Yes, I could have disputed the charge with my credit card company, but why should a customer have to go through that headache immediately after making what they understood to be a reservation? I have used online booking services expecting transparency about when I will be charged and what cancellation or modification conditions apply. I will never book with them again.

Review Title: I would strongly advise against booking…
Review Text: I would strongly advise against booking flights through Booking.com based on my experience. I booked flights and was told they would take a couple of hours to process. Two days later, I still had no confirmation email, and the payment was still showing as pending. Trying to contact customer service was incredibly frustrating. The phone numbers either rang out or led to an AI system that asked for a confirmation code I had never received, meaning I couldn’t get through to anyone. I was repeatedly directed to the online help page, which offered no useful assistance whatsoever. I also sent numerous emails to customer service, only to receive the same automated AI-generated responses over and over again. This caused unnecessary stress while I was trying to organise my holiday, including accommodation, transfers, and activities. After several days with no meaningful support, I eventually contacted Booking.com through Instagram. They finally provided a phone number where I was able to speak to a real person. I was then told that my flights had never been processed. There was no apology and, more importantly, no email, phone call, or any other attempt to inform me that the booking had failed. Had I not continued chasing this myself, I could have turned up expecting to travel without ever having valid flights. Thankfully, there were still seats available, but that may not have been the case. This experience was stressful, time-consuming, and completely unacceptable. I have lost all confidence in Booking.com and will never book flights through them again. If you’re considering using Booking.com for flights, I would recommend booking directly with the airline instead to avoid the risk of being left without a confirmed booking or any meaningful customer support.

Review Title: DO NOT USE BOOKING.COM
Review Text: When my reservation was processed, Booking.com incorrectly classified one of the youth travelers in my party as an "unaccompanied minor" and charged an additional fee of $194 for a service that was neither requested nor available through the airline. As well as charged me for seat reservations $49.90 per person. After the booking was completed, the airline contacted me directly to advise that this reservation was invalid because they do not offer unaccompanied minor services. As a result of the error made during the booking process, the airline was forced to cancel the entire reservation for all five travelers. The airline also confirmed that even though booking charged and collected payment for reserved seats, they did not reserve them with the airline. This cancellation created substantial inconvenience and financial hardship. I spent approximately four hours working with the airline to rebook travel arrangements that should not have been disrupted in the first place. The situation caused unnecessary stress and required significant time and effort to resolve. To support my claim, I have submitted multiple written complaints and provided documentation, including: Copies of the original booking confirmation Documentation Written communications from the airline confirming that the reservation was improperly booked Evidence that the airline canceled the reservation as a direct result of the booking error Despite submitting this information on three separate occasions, I have not received a meaningful response or reimbursement from Booking.com.

Review Title: DO NOT BOOK FLIGHTS
Review Text: Classic - if I could put 0 stars I would. I booked return flights to Vietnam through Dubai in January this year. Now I totally understand that flight were disrupted because of the war in Iran. Booking.com or really ‘gotogate’ contacted me to ask if I wanted to change my flights or get a refund. I chose the refund option as I had a limited time in Vietnam due to time off and the new flight didn’t match up with hotels book. I was told that my refund would be with me in 14 days. Fine - I booked another flight. I go on the trip and come back and it’s not been a month or so and still no money. I contacted booking.com customer service multiple times all giving me different answers. One woman even said there was not time limit on refunds - I asked her okay so I have to wait a year - 10 years (as a joke) and she said maybe. The trip was end of march- April. I continued to contact them through April and into may and eventually I had to contact my bank which is how I finally got the refund IN JUNE. They offered me a refund in Feb/ march time. Hotel experience has been okay with booking.com but DO NOT BOOK FLIGHTS. I’ve learnt my lesson and I will always booked through the airline even if it is more expensive. I thought as booking.com is usually very reputable that they would be okay but never again. The only response I ever got was we are waiting for the airline. However I contact the airline direct and they basically told me they have issued it to booking.com and could not do anything else on their end. BE AWARE THEY ALSO USE GOTOGATE so this review is also for them.

Review Text: NEVER HIRE A CAR THROUGH BOOKING.COM!! I had an accident when a Wallaby ran out in front of the vehicle, as well as injuring the animal it caused £1500 worth of cosmetic damage to the car. As the insurance was through a third party, I had to pay SIXT $6000 bond to cover the damage, wait weeks to get the balance back once they had repaired the vehicle and then weeks again to finally get my claim paid to me. This whole process took over 3 months and a lot of time and many, many emails, as well as stress and inconvenience. The whole process was flawed from start to finish, terrible communication and awful customer service. I will be cancelling my Booking.com account and never using them again. Review Title: ★ 1 Star
Review Text: ★ 1 Star — DoorDash Completely Ignored a Serious App Problem and Penalized Me for It I’ve completed nearly 5,000 deliveries as a Dasher and have maintained a 95%+ acceptance rate and Platinum Dasher status. I know how the DoorDash app is supposed to work, which makes what happened—and DoorDash’s complete lack of response—even more frustrating. On July 28th, I started dashing and was hit with 15 timed-out orders. The problem? The assignments NEVER showed up on my phone. They didn't appear on my screen for me to accept or decline. I never saw the restaurants, the payout, the distance, or any other information about these orders. They simply weren't there. I couldn't accept them. I couldn't decline them. I never even had the opportunity to make a decision because DoorDash never delivered the assignments to my phone. And to be clear, this isn't a case of me using some outdated phone that can't handle the DoorDash app. I have a current, top-of-the-line smartphone with 5G capabilities, with more than enough capability to run the DoorDash app. I've completed nearly 5,000 deliveries using the platform. I immediately contacted DoorDash multiple times and explained exactly what was happening. I was told they would investigate the issue. I actually stopped dashing for 10 days to give DoorDash time to figure out what was wrong before I tried again. During those 10 days, all I received were generic, form-letter responses essentially saying, “Here's your reference number, and we're looking into it.” Apparently, they weren't looking into anything. On August 7th, I tried dashing again, and the exact same thing happened. This time I caught the problem after another 5 assignments timed out, bringing my total to 20 timed-out orders. Twenty orders. NONE of these were declined orders. I did not decline them. The assignments never showed up on my phone. Some of these were high-paying orders. Some were very short, easy deliveries that I would have gladly accepted. I never even got the chance to see them. Yet DoorDash's system apparently considers all 20 of these as though I intentionally chose not to accept them. The result? My acceptance rate went from over 95% down to 76%, putting my Platinum Dasher status at risk. I've contacted DoorDash repeatedly. I've explained the problem. I've given them the dates. I've provided the reference numbers. I've stopped dashing for 10 days while they supposedly investigated. Then I tried again and experienced the exact same technical failure. And what has DoorDash done? Nothing. They refuse to properly investigate the technical problem. They refuse to correct the 20 timed-out assignments. They refuse to restore my acceptance rate. And they refuse to restore the Platinum status that I earned through thousands of deliveries. After nearly 5,000 dashes, I know the difference between an order I intentionally decline and an order that never appears on my phone in the first place. If DoorDash's system fails to deliver an assignment to a Dasher's phone, the Dasher should not be penalized for it. I did everything I was supposed to do. I reported the problem. I stopped working for 10 days to give them time to investigate. I tried again, and the exact same problem happened. I've repeatedly contacted support, and instead of actually fixing the problem, I've been given generic responses and reference numbers. At this point, I have no confidence that anyone at DoorDash is actually investigating my situation. DoorDash needs to take responsibility for its own technology instead of making Dashers pay the price for technical failures that are completely outside of their control. Nearly 5,000 deliveries, a top-of-the-line 5G phone, a history of maintaining a 95%+ acceptance rate, and Platinum status—and apparently none of that matters when their system fails and their support team refuses to fix it. If you're considering becoming a Dasher, understand that when something goes wrong with the DoorDash app, you may be completely on your own. Extremely disappointed in DoorDash and their support. One star is generous.

Review Title: ⭐ 1 STAR
Review Text: ⭐ 1 STAR — DoorDash is NOT what you think it is After using DoorDash repeatedly, I have to say that my experience has been extremely disappointing. Food frequently arrives late, cold, damaged, or poorly handled. And when there is a problem with the driver, getting meaningful help from DoorDash can be incredibly frustrating. We have had drivers leave food without asking for the required delivery code. We have also had situations where the driver was late, the food was cold, and the pizza arrived crushed. One incident went far beyond a bad delivery. We contacted DoorDash while the driver was still involved, and the driver became belligerent and cursed at me while DoorDash was on the phone. He was more concerned with leaving to make another delivery than addressing the fact that our order had arrived late and damaged. The situation became serious enough that a police report had to be filed. What made it even more frustrating was DoorDash telling us that they couldn’t do anything because the driver was working through a third-party arrangement. That raises a very basic question: Who is actually responsible when something goes wrong? DoorDash charges customers delivery fees, service fees, membership fees, and encourages tipping. Customers are essentially being asked to absorb more and more of the cost while the delivery experience can still be terrible. And then there are the confusing options where you’re asked to pay extra if you want your order delivered immediately rather than having it bundled or delayed. If I’m already paying delivery and service fees, why should I have to pay even more just to receive the food I already ordered in a reasonable amount of time? The biggest problem is accountability. When everything goes smoothly, DoorDash gets paid. But when something goes wrong, suddenly everyone has an excuse — the restaurant, the driver, the third-party company, or the customer. DoorDash needs to take responsibility for the entire delivery experience, not just the transaction. At the end of the day, DoorDash doesn’t feel like a reliable delivery service. It feels like a middleman collecting fees while customers are left dealing with the consequences when the system fails. My advice: think twice before ordering. The fees aren’t worth it if your food arrives late, cold, crushed, or you can’t get meaningful help when something goes wrong.

Review Title: Unreliable drivers, zero accountability, and rising costs—I’m done with DoorDash.
Review Text: I used to rely on DoorDash regularly, but the recent, rapid decline in service quality—paired with constantly escalating fees—has made it completely impossible to justify using this platform anymore. Between drivers mishandling orders and DoorDash refusing to take responsibility, the overall experience has become consistently frustrating. Three recent experiences in a row demonstrate just how bad it’s gotten: Instance 1 (Delivered someone else’s food): A driver completely mixed up orders and dropped off the wrong food while I was at work. Because of their carelessness, I was left without a lunch for the rest of my workday. Instance 2 (40-minute grocery detour with my hot food): A driver picked up our restaurant order, but instead of bringing it to us, drove to a nearby Kroger and spent 40 minutes inside doing personal shopping or running another errand. The food arrived nearly an hour late and completely cold. When I reached out to DoorDash, they passed the buck and claimed they couldn't do anything because the order was placed through the restaurant’s app—leaving the local restaurant to take the financial hit and remake the food for a mistake the DoorDash driver made. Instance 3 (Prioritizing distant deliveries over a 1-mile route): I ordered smoothies from a location just one mile from my office. The driver picked up my order, bypassed my office entirely, and drove significantly farther away to complete another delivery first. By the time my drinks were dropped off, they were completely melted into warm liquid. It is ridiculous that customers are charged premium markups, service fees, and delivery charges only to receive melted drinks, cold food, or no lunch at all. DoorDash treats its customers and partner restaurants as collateral damage while taking no accountability for driver negligence. I will no longer be giving DoorDash my business, and I strongly recommend ordering directly from local restaurants or using alternative services that actually value their customers.

Review Title: Title: Repeated documented issues and no confidence in DoorDash’s resolution process
Review Text: 7/21/26 I have been a regular DoorDash customer, and I don’t write negative reviews lightly. Unfortunately, after several documented issues over the past few weeks, I no longer have confidence in DoorDash’s customer support or escalation process. My concerns began with multiple Starbucks deliveries from one location where my Frappuccinos repeatedly arrived significantly underfilled and often melted. I documented these deliveries with photographs because the issue became recurring. I reported these problems through DoorDash, but I did not feel they were resolved appropriately. I eventually switched to a different Starbucks location, and the difference was immediate. My Frappuccinos arrived properly frozen, much closer to the expected fill level, and the espresso was noticeably stronger. That confirmed to me that the drink quality issue appeared to be specific to that Starbucks location—not every Starbucks. However, what never improved was DoorDash’s handling of customer service. On July 21, 2026, I placed a DoorDash Starbucks order that was marked as delivered, but I never received my food. I contacted DoorDash multiple times and was told my case had been escalated to a specialized team. I never received any follow-up, refund, or resolution. After waiting, I ultimately had to file a PayPal dispute, which is still pending. Then, on August 1, 2026, I ordered dinner from another restaurant through DoorDash. I paid for two extra tzatziki sauces, but they were missing from the sealed bag. I was not asking for a refund of my meal—I requested reimbursement only for the missing paid add-on. DoorDash’s automated system immediately denied my request. Because of my previous unresolved experience, I called customer support instead of relying on the app. The representative was courteous and professional, and I appreciate the way they treated me. However, I was once again told my case would be escalated to a specialized team—the same process that never resulted in a follow-up on my previous case. My frustration isn’t about $1.50. It’s about confidence in the support process. Restaurants make mistakes. Drivers cannot verify the contents of sealed bags. I understand that. What I don’t understand is why customers who document legitimate problems, report them promptly, and ask only for reimbursement of missing paid items are left feeling that their concerns disappear into an escalation process with no meaningful follow-up. I sincerely hope DoorDash improves both its automated refund system and its escalation process because customers deserve to know that documented issues will actually be reviewed and resolved.

Review Title: The restrictions of netflix
Review Text: I really enjoy the variety of content Netflix offers, and it's one of my favourite streaming services. However, I frequently encounter a significant issue when travelling internationally. Whenever I visit another country, the available subtitles automatically switch to the local language, and there is no option to change them back to English. This makes it impossible for me to watch non-English content, such as anime and Southeast Asian dramas, because English subtitles are no longer available. Unfortunately, using a VPN is not a solution, as Netflix detects it and prevents playback until it is turned off. I believe Netflix should allow users to choose subtitle languages based on their personal preferences rather than their current location. I think it would greatly improve the experience using this app that I pay for. At the moment, this limitation prevents me from watching many of my favourite shows while travelling, which significantly reduces the value of my subscription during those periods. I hope Netflix will consider introducing a global subtitle preference, as I believe it would greatly benefit many users.

Review Title: Netflix is one of the most popular…
Review Text: Netflix is one of the most popular streaming services and offering a wide variety of movies, TV shows, documentaries, and original series. It has something for almost everyone, which is one reason it became so successful. The platform is easy to use, works well on TVs, phones, tablets, and computers, and provides personalized recommendations based on what viewers watch. At first, Netflix leaves a good impression because finding content is simple to use and the streaming quality is usually reliable with a stable internet connection. Although Netflix has many positive features, many viewers feel the service has changed over the years, and not necessarily for the better. One of the biggest frustrations is spending more time scrolling through titles than actually finding something worth watching. While Netflix continues to release original movies and series, not all of them are enjoyable, and many popular shows seem to get canceled just when viewers become invested in the story. This can leave subscribers feeling disappointed after spending time following a series that never gets a proper ending. Another downside is the price. Subscription costs have continued to increase, making many subscribers question whether the service is still worth the money. At the same time, several popular movies and television shows have been removed from the platform, giving viewers fewer familiar options to choose from. The password-sharing restrictions also frustrated many longtime subscribers who were used to sharing accounts with close family members. While Netflix still offers convenience and has a few great original shows, many viewers feel other streaming services give them more for what they're paying. Overall, Netflix receives 2 out of 5 stars in this review. The platform is easy to navigate and still offers quality streaming, but the rising subscription costs, changing content library, and frequent cancellation of popular shows make it difficult to recommend. Netflix may still be a good option for people who enjoy binge-watching original series and don’t mind the possibility of not getting an ending, However, anyone looking for the best value and a larger variety of movies and shows may be happier with another streaming service.

Review Title: Spotify is a vGreat for listeners, frustrating for independent artistsery strong platform from…
Review Text: Spotify is a very strong platform from a listener’s perspective: it is convenient, easy to use, offers a huge music library, and has become one of the main places where people discover and listen to music. From the perspective of an independent artist, however, my experience is much more disappointing. Spotify gives the impression of reach and visibility, but in practice very little of that turns into real support or sustainable growth. Streams generate extremely low income, older achievements quickly lose visibility, follower numbers feel unstable, and without additional marketing money almost nothing happens. The problem is not Spotify alone, but the whole system around it. Artists create the music, invest time, money and energy, while platforms, distributors, labels and marketing services benefit far more from the structure. For independent musicians, this can easily become frustrating: you keep working, hoping and investing, but the system rarely gives much back. For listeners, Spotify is excellent. For independent artists, it can be deeply discouraging, unfair and exhausting.

Review Title: I subscribed to a Premium Family plan…
Review Text: I subscribed to a Premium Family plan on Spotify and included three users in my account. Everything was functioning normally until, without any warning or clear reason, I suddenly lost access to my account after just 13 days of use. When I contacted support, I was informed that my account had been closed. However, no explanation was provided, and I was explicitly told that no further information could be shared. This lack of transparency is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about how user accounts are handled. Even more concerning is the way the support process was handled. I was kept in a support chat for nearly an hour, repeatedly transferred between different agents, and ultimately left without any resolution. The case was effectively closed without addressing my concerns. All of my playlists and years of saved music have become inaccessible due to this action. This is not just a minor service issue—it reflects a serious failure in user data access and account management responsibilities. At this point, I intend to escalate this matter to relevant consumer protection authorities and pursue formal complaints through appropriate legal channels. I also believe this situation highlights the need for closer regulatory scrutiny of platform practices regarding account termination and user data access. This issue should not be ignored, as it reflects a broader concern about accountability and user rights on digital platforms.

Review Title: I am extremely unhappy with my…
Review Text: I am extremely unhappy with my experience with Temu and honestly feel let down as a customer. I placed an order, paid for it, and waited for it to arrive. The tracking then stated that my parcel had been “delivered.” The problem is that I DID NOT RECEIVE MY ORDER. It was apparently left outside, unattended, without being handed to me or placed somewhere secure. How can an order be considered successfully delivered when the customer has not received it? I understand that delivery companies can have problems, but leaving a paid parcel outside and simply marking it as delivered is not an acceptable solution. Once a parcel is left unattended, it can easily disappear, be stolen, damaged by weather, or be taken by somebody else. The customer should not be expected to take responsibility for that. I paid for my items in good faith and expected them to arrive safely. Instead, I am left without my order and having to deal with the frustration of contacting customer service and explaining something that should be very straightforward: I ordered it, I paid for it, and I did not receive it. The fact that the tracking says “delivered” does not magically mean I received the package. There is a huge difference between a parcel being marked as delivered and a customer actually receiving it. This has completely changed my opinion of Temu. Before this experience, I was willing to order from the platform, but now I have serious concerns about whether my orders will actually reach me safely. Customers should not have to worry that their purchases will simply be left outside and potentially disappear. Temu needs to take delivery problems much more seriously and make sure customers are properly protected when an order is not received. I am extremely disappointed and expect Temu to take responsibility for this situation and provide a proper resolution. I paid for an order that I never received, and that is simply not acceptable. Based on this experience, I would seriously reconsider ordering from Temu again. Very poor experience and very frustrating customer service

Review Title: Temu Has Me
Review Text: I, like many shoppers, avoided Temu for years because I wasn't sure if it was legitimate. I now regret that. They have a huge variety of things at great prices, and for the most part the quality is good. I do think they have far too many wild games and promotions which really are just confusing to use, and are borderline fraudulent. However the price adjustment feature on orders is great. You can request a price adjustment on anything you order for up to 30 days from the time you order it and they'll give it to you, even if you do it every single day for 30 days. This can add up to a lot of credits. If you're going to use Temu, you need to learn how to request price adjustments. My only real complaint about Temu, and this is consistent among many different kinds of things I've ordered from them, they misrepresent the size of things, sometimes in the written dimensions and sometimes what they show in pictures of the product. Usually things are smaller than they say they are. I've learned over time how much to assume they are too small so that I order things that I need in the right size, but it's awkward and they really need to address that. I don't really understand why they take that approach though because most people know what size they need of a particular product and that's what they want and that's what they're expecting. It just leads to returns of items for refunds when you get something that is not the dimensions you need. I'm going to continue to use Temu. I hear people say they're Communist and they steal your data, and all this and that, but I figure data stealing is probably happening with anything I buy from anybody online, and I'm certainly not going to stop shopping online, the economic benefits are too good.

Review Title: Absolutely terrible customer support…
Review Text: Absolutely terrible customer support experience with Uber. I lost an item during a trip and was trying to confirm whether an item the driver found was actually mine. Uber sent me an email asking me to confirm the item, but there was no message or picture visible, so I had no way to identify it. I spent hours trying to get a clear answer through support. I was repeatedly told that my request would be transferred to a “specialized team,” with no clear explanation of what that meant or how long I would have to wait. I specifically asked whether I needed to keep checking the app or whether someone would contact me, but still couldn't get a straightforward answer. The final support agent acknowledged my concern, repeated the standard warning that Uber and the driver aren't responsible for lost items, and then closed the chat while I was still trying to get an answer. That felt incredibly dismissive and rude. I understand that Uber cannot guarantee recovery of a lost item, and I wasn't asking them to magically find it. I simply wanted to confirm whether the item was mine and understand what I was supposed to do next. Instead, I was transferred around, left waiting, and ultimately had the conversation closed without resolving the actual issue. For a company of Uber's size, this is an unnecessarily frustrating customer support experience. The problem isn't just the lost item, the lack of clear communication and the way the support interaction was handled is what made this experience so bad.

Review Text: Uber locked changes to my account over an unexplained $50 USD charge. I repeatedly told them I believed it was related to a fraudulent gift card transaction I had reported in April, which my bank fortunately blocked. Instead of answers, I kept receiving generic responses telling me they were happy to help and that I simply needed to pay the $50 to unlock my account. They suggested someone had obtained my login credentials, despite my account already having a complex, randomly generated, unique password and 2FA. Then Uber contacted me again and finally confirmed what I had been telling them all along: the $50 was the fraudulent gift card purchase from April that I had already reported. It was never a trip. Review Title: Uber has become increasingly unreliable…
Review Text: Uber has become increasingly unreliable and inconvenient. The app frequently cancels rides internally, has payment processing issues, takes too long to match riders with drivers, and often forces customers to verify their payment at the worst possible time—when they’re rushing to the airport, heading to an important business meeting, trying to catch a flight, or simply needing to arrive somewhere on time. It has gotten to the point where you can’t depend on Uber anymore. This isn’t just an inconvenience—it can have serious consequences. Someone fleeing a domestic violence situation or facing another emergency could be put at risk because of delays, unnecessary payment verification requests, or canceled rides. On top of that, Uber’s customer service is extremely disappointing. It’s nearly impossible to reach a real person, and customers are instead directed through AI responses and automated email systems that rarely resolve the issue. This is one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve encountered. Uber needs to improve the reliability of its platform, fix its payment and ride-booking issues, and provide customers with access to real human support. Until then, I can no longer rely on Uber for transportation when it matters most.

Review Title: Lousy customer service
Review Text: First things first. This is NOT a review of the Uber service or the app. It's a review of their customer service. I tried to create an account on the Uber app. Upon entering my email address, I got an error message saying that my account had been suspended. I submitted a written (typed) message asking how I could possibly be suspended since I've never had an account before. A customer service representative (who might have been a person or might have been an AI bot) sent a reply that began with "Dear Kalaya," and proceeded to tell me that I was suspended because I had misused their service. Which was a problem since my name is Kelly. But that told me that this Kalaya person had an account that used MY email instead of her own. Relevant background: This happens to me all the time. As an early adopter of Gmail, I was able to get "kjones[at]gmail[dot]com" (Jones is not my real last name). So anybody whose first name began with K and whose last name was the same as mine had to add a middle initial, a number, etc. as their email address. Some of them forget they did this, and at some later time, they erroneously give their email as "kjones[at]gmail[dot]com. As a result, I get email intended for other people all the time. I've gotten doctor's appointment reminders, messages from children's school teacher, condo association minutes, invoices for flying lessons, Atlanta Falcons e-tickets, and most recently, reminders to pick up an order from a Bath & Body Works store. If I am able and have the time, I contact the sender, explain the situation, and they apologize and remove my email address. I explained all this to Uber's customer service rep/bot and asked that they release my email from their system so I could use it for myself. Their reply: "Dear Kalaya,... We will not be lifting your suspension." This went back and forth a couple more times until the rep/bot finally acknowledged that I was not Kalaya. But they still won't let me sign up. I simply cannot understand how anybody could be so obtuse and yet work in customer service. I'll give their competitor my business instead.

I only found this out through a formal data protection request under UK GDPR, years later, and only after Wise missed multiple legal deadlines to answer me. My money is gone. My account is closed. My case is closed. And the decision was made using material nobody checked. I am not writing this out of anger alone. I am writing it because I have it in writing, and because anyone trusting Wise with their money deserves to know how a dispute can be handled when it goes wrong. I have not forgotten. Review Title: The “Cancel” button does NOT mean your…
Review Text: The “Cancel” button does NOT mean your transfer is cancelled immediately I am very disappointed with Wise’s cancellation process. The interface gives the impression that cancelling a transfer is as simple as clicking “Cancel.” However, cancellation is apparently not immediate. I was informed that it can take up to two working days to process the cancellation. That means the situation is very different from what the cancellation button suggests: you may click cancel, but your money can remain tied up for up to two working days while you wait for the cancellation to actually be completed. This is a serious issue when dealing with money. If a customer decides they need to cancel a transfer, they may reasonably expect the cancellation to happen promptly and the funds to become available again. Instead, they can be left waiting for days. I believe Wise should make this limitation clearly and prominently visible before the customer confirms the cancellation. A simple “Cancel” button without an obvious warning that the process may take up to two working days creates an impression of immediate cancellation that does not match the actual process. Financial services should be transparent about when customers will regain access to their money. Two working days is not a minor detail — it can be financially significant. Wise may provide a convenient transfer service, but the cancellation process needs much greater transparency. Customers should not have to discover only after clicking “Cancel” that their money may remain unavailable for up to two working days. My advice to anyone using Wise: before sending a transfer, be aware that cancelling it may not be an immediate process, and your money may remain tied up while the cancellation is being processed.
